definitions: Marketing page

One agreed URL with a defined audience, purpose and approved outline, using an agreed page type. Home, individual service, about, contact and proof pages count. Researched practical guide

One buyer question answered through an approved outline, client expertise and bounded desk research, with sources checked and linked. Depth is set by the question rather than word count. It differs from a standard service page by its research and explanatory purpose. Included Business/Signature guides use page slots. A guide in Local Search Partnership consumes its two monthly content/SEO units. No ranking guarantee.
Policy page
Up to three client-approved policy texts can be formatted outside a website plan's marketing-page cap. W&M is not being hired to draft legal policies or determine their adequacy.
Content collection entry

A supplied record placed into an agreed reusable template, such as a project or team member. Collection-entry limits are separate from marketing pages because original writing and unique design are not included for each entry. A separately written entry uses a marketing-page allocation or module.

Revision round

One compiled feedback list from one approver for the current stage, followed by one implementation pass. Refinement within the agreed direction is included; a different concept, new audience or added functionality is a change request. Correcting a defect is not a paid revision round.
Acceptance
Completion of the named deliverables and written tests, followed by explicit client approval. Silence is not treated as launch permission.
Defect

A delivered item failing the agreed acceptance criteria because of W&M's implementation. Correct it without using a client's monthly output allowance. New preferences, new requirements and subsequent third-party changes are different work.
Complete project hours

Include discovery, research, copy, design, production, QA, calls, messages, revisions, handoff and expected defect correction. Internal hours help price scope; they are not a hidden limit that lets W&M abandon an agreed fixed deliverable.
Writing scope without word caps

Agree the page purpose, topic/question, available evidence, research method, deliverables and review rounds before booking. The agreed research is client facts plus ordinary desk/query research; original interviews, surveys, specialist legal/scientific research or additional topics require a separate scope. W&M absorbs its own underestimation. Extra length required for the unchanged approved purpose does not trigger a fee.
delivery_policies: Readiness and queue

Allow roughly one week for collecting inputs as an initial planning allowance, but do not promise that client-controlled readiness has a fixed duration. State the next available start separately from the plan's active delivery range.
Owner work and elapsed time

The quoted calendar is not a billable-hour claim. Short builds can finish earlier by explicit agreement after every gate passes. Do not promise same-day or four-hour delivery from the owner’s internal estimate. Readiness and the sales queue remain separate from the booked delivery window.
Working calendar

Project weeks are calendar weeks, with work scheduled Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm America/New_York, excluding announced holidays. Project day ranges are business days. Days in a monthly cycle are calendar days of that billing cycle; schedule actual work/reviews on business days.
Feedback

Plan for consolidated feedback within two business days at each gate. Normal review time is included in the planned range; the shortest endpoint requires the prompt approvals stated in that plan. Agree longer review windows before booking.
Weekly update
For active projects, send one weekly update with completed work, preview/evidence, decisions needed, blockers and the next dated milestone. This is included delivery work.
Calls are optional

Written intake, approvals, review and support are the default for every plan/module. All W&M interviews, workshops, sessions, training and walkthroughs elsewhere mean written exchanges plus recorded demonstrations, with the stated appointment available by choice. The appointment substitutes for the corresponding exchange; it does not stack unlimited additional consulting. Provide the same decisions, instructions and acceptance evidence either way. Vendor identity/video verification can still be required by the vendor.
Questions and incidents

Send email or messages through the agreed text channel at any time, including nights/weekends. During active projects, paid monthly service and applicable clarification/defect windows, acknowledge within one business day, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm America/New_York excluding announced holidays. Give the next action and a separate resolution estimate. Care site-down/failed-checkout reports receive triage within one business day. Messages are not continuously monitored; 24/7 submission is not 24/7 staffing, instant response or unlimited new work.
Client delay

Notify the owner when a missing decision threatens a milestone. After five business days beyond the agreed response deadline, issue a pause notice and release the production slot. Resume at the next mutually agreed slot with a new date; do not silently continue charging project labor for waiting.
Change requests

State the requested change, exact deliverable, additional fee and schedule effect. Obtain written agreement before doing it. An internal under-estimate of unchanged agreed scope is W&M's responsibility.
W&M delay

Notify promptly, keep the agreed scope, provide a dated recovery plan and offer the appropriate reschedule/credit/refund for work not delivered. Do not blame the client for an unrecorded internal capacity problem.
Launch control
Launch only after explicit approval and the named acceptance checks. Preserve the agreed rollback path and avoid moving DNS, email or live payments without the owner-approved cutover plan.
Post-launch

For website/store builds, check within two business days and around day 14. Defect-reporting windows: Focused/Store 30 days; Custom/Business 60; Signature 90. Timely reported defects remain covered until corrected. Business/Signature include one bounded day-30 review of launch observations, no new campaign.
No silent service substitution
If an included tool or platform capability proves unavailable, explain the limitation and agree an equivalent deliverable or revised scope/fee before treating the project as complete.

All monthly deliverables must finish within the paid billing cycle, including February and other short cycles. Schedule review, QA and reporting on business days by cycle end; a numbered stage never extends the paid cycle automatically.

Apply the relevant shared checks to every website/store build and to the pages, configurations and journeys changed by Repair, Workflow, monthly production and standalone modules. A module does not include an unrelated whole-site audit. Tests must still cover any shared component it changes.

Reconcile the signed page/form/collection inventory. Check approved business facts, titles, descriptions, headings, links, image alt text and permissioned assets. Verify the client-approved policy texts are present.

40% to reserve the agreed start, 30% after approval of copy/design direction, and 30% after staging acceptance before the scheduled launch. Show dollar amounts and milestone definitions in the proposal. No production work starts without agreed scope and initial payment.

50% at booking and 50% on delivery/acceptance of the agreed output. Local Presence Setup's final milestone is completion of the specified work and handoff, not a platform verification outcome.
